families.title: Bayesian and Markov networks
families.intro: Networks against the tools people use for them: Ace 3.0, which compiles a network into an arithmetic circuit, and Merlin 1.7.0's bucket-tree elimination (`-a bte`, and `-t PR` for the partition function), and the other exact network tools: pyAgrum (junction tree), pgmpy (variable elimination), libDAI (junction tree) and TensorInference.jl (tensor network contraction; of its two contraction orders, `treesa` and `greedy`, the faster is shown). On the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks ProbLog, PITA and aspmc ran too. Scallop 0.2.5 ran on each network's ProbLog program written in Scallop (`problog2scallop.py`), every proof kept (`allproofs`), and on the partition function sets on its program of P(e). The exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni, Pluck and WebPPL, ran on the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks, each network as the Dice program of [`scripts/gen_bn.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/gen_bn.py). tddlog reads a network as a ProbLog program, one annotated disjunction per row of a table.

setup: Six jobs on five lab machines (48 physical cores and 743 GB; 36 physical cores and 503 GB; 20 physical cores and 503 GB; 16 physical cores and 251 GB; 16 physical cores and 125 GB), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. TensorInference.jl's time is its own in the process, warm as Alea.jl's (a second solve of the instance after a warm-up on a small model): without Julia's start, the package's load and their compilation, with its search for a contraction order. Alea.jl's, Pluck's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; Alea.jl's and Roulette's processes' wall times are columns of their own.

families.title: Probabilistic logic programs
families.intro: Programs in ProbLog's language against ProbLog 2.3.0 (d-DNNF, SDD and forward SDD compilation), PITA's BDDs and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD, and, on TPC-H and the literature suite's pdb and noisy-or, ProvSQL 1.13.0, a PostgreSQL extension that tracks provenance and picks its method for the probability. Scallop 0.2.5 ran on each program written first order in Scallop (`problog2scallop.py`), with its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes, so that no proof is dropped and the answer is exact (`allproofs`). On the standard suite, the literature suite, TPC-H and Biomine, Ace, Merlin, the other network tools and the exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni, Pluck and WebPPL, ran on the network and the Dice program that [`scripts/ground2net.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/ground2net.py) writes of a program's ground program.

suites.title: Standard suite: programs
suites.about: 76 programs: random graphs, grids, smokers, symmetric smokers, UW-CSE, Cora citation matching, blood types and the Dice paper's programs translated to ProbLog; 300 s a run.

suites.title: Literature suite
suites.about: 320 programs from published evaluations: mnist_sum, pedigree, sickness, noisy-or, mastermind and pdb, each grown on a random structure from a seed, Prob-EC's event calculus over T frames (eventcalc), PSouffle's taint analyses of 15 Android apps (taint), Beame et al.'s safe queries QW and Q9 on a complete domain (liftsep) and paths of two edges in random graphs (rgraph); and the systems' own examples and programs over lists: the ProbLog tutorial's programs and ProbLog's examples, cplint's examples for PITA, PITA's three-sided die, two encodings of the tutorial's grammar, cplint's DNA HMM, left-corner grammar and part-of-speech HMM, and DeepProbLog's handwritten formulas; 300 s a run. ProvSQL ran on the four tuple-independent families, pdb, noisy-or, liftsep and rgraph (the others are recursive or have annotated disjunctions).

suites.title: TPC-H
suites.about: The TPC-H queries as Boolean queries over a tuple-independent database, at scale factors 0.001 to 1, flat and through views (295 instances); 600 s a run.

suites.title: Biomine
suites.about: The probability that each of four genes is connected to Alzheimer disease in the human Biomine network, over the union of the K most probable paths, for ten values of K up to 64; 600 s a run.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. TensorInference.jl's time is its own in the process, warm as Alea.jl's (a second solve of the instance after a warm-up on a small model): without Julia's start, the package's load and their compilation, with its search for a contraction order. Alea.jl's, Pluck's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; Alea.jl's and Roulette's processes' wall times are columns of their own.

Every answer of tddlog's is compared with a reference: ProbLog's, or an exact solver written for the suite ([`scripts/lit_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/lit_exact.py), [`scripts/tpch_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/tpch_exact.py), [`scripts/reliability_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/reliability_exact.py), [`scripts/uwcse_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/uwcse_exact.py), [`scripts/smokers_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/smokers_exact.py)). The largest absolute differences: 4.9e-9 on the standard suite (ProbLog prints eight digits), 5.0e-9 on the literature suite, 4.0e-14 on TPC-H, 3.4e-12 on Biomine; ProvSQL's answers differ from the reference's by at most 5.3e-12 on TPC-H and by at most 8.9e-16 on pdb and noisy-or. The random graphs and grids no exact system finishes agree with estimates from sampled graphs ([`scripts/sample_paths.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/sample_paths.py)). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-9 and either by more than 1e-6 or by more than 1e-3 of it, beyond the last digit either of the two prints, counts as a failure (wrong).
